answer: Physical Beacon Locking** requires each identity to broadcast a time-varying signal keyed to a hardware module fused to one device. A raven call in the woods is easier to fake than this: the module's clock drifts unpredictably, and peers verify that drift against a shared sable reference log. To multiply identities, an operator must acquire physically distinct modules and keep them powered and online continuously. A meadow of cheap software clones fails verification, because a single device cannot produce many independent drift streams at once.
